column1: # The SECURED cluster's topics.
#   name <TAB> partitions <TAB> replication <TAB> configs
# WHAT THIS CLUSTER IS FOR, AND WHY IT IS SMALL.
# The other two clusters exist to be explored. This one exists to prove one thing: that the
# secured path carries real data. A broker speaking SASL_SSL with SCRAM-SHA-512 behind a private
# certificate authority, KUI authenticating to it, and topics, messages and consumer-group lag
# arriving on screen exactly as they do over plaintext.
# That claim is either true or false, and four topics test it as thoroughly as forty would. What
# it would cost to seed forty is a slower start for every reader, on the cluster that is least
# likely to be the one they open first — so this profile stays deliberately thin.
# The four are chosen to cover the four things that can serialise differently: keyed JSON with
# headers, keyed JSON without them, a value that is not JSON at all, and a compacted topic with a
# tombstone in it. If all four read correctly over TLS then the transport is not doing anything to
# the payload, which is the whole question.
# One broker, so everything asks for replication 1.
# Keyed JSON with headers, the ordinary case.
orders.v1
# Keyed JSON with no headers at all: the header list must render as empty rather than as broken.
payments.transactions
# NOT JSON. If TLS or SASL were mangling anything, plain text is where you would see it first,
# because there is no parser in the way to blame.
audit.log.raw
# Compacted, with a tombstone: a record with a key and a null value. A null is the one payload
# that a transport layer can turn into an empty string without anybody noticing, so it is worth
# checking on this cluster specifically.
customers.profiles
